subtopics.title: What a Tariff Is and Who Charges One

questions.question: A tariff is best described as:
options: The total amount of a municipal bill
A price charged per unit of a service used

questions.question: A tariff that charges a higher price for each successive block of consumption is called:
A fixed or basic charge on a municipal account is payable:
options: Only when consumption is above the first block
Only in months with high usage
Only if the account is in arrears
Every month, even if consumption is zero

questions.question: Municipalities use rising block tariffs mainly to:
options: Keep basic usage affordable while charging heavy users more per unit
Make every unit cost the same for all households
Reward households that use the most electricity

subtopics.title: Rising Block Electricity: Filling the Blocks in Order

questions.question: With block one at R2,20 for the first 100 kWh, the cost of those 100 kWh is:
For 380 kWh, the number of units charged in block two (101 to 400 kWh at R2,60) is:
The total prepaid cost for 380 kWh on the given rising block tariff is:
Charging all 380 units at the block-two rate of R2,60 is wrong because:
options: The block-two rate only applies above 650 kWh
VAT must be added before multiplying
380 units never fit into block two
Each block's rate applies only to the units inside that block

subtopics.title: Water Tariffs and the Free Basic Allowance

questions.question: Free basic water in the lesson's tariff means:
options: The first 6 kl each month cost R0
All water is free below R404,00
The first 15 kl each month cost R0

questions.question: For 22 kl, the charge for the block from 6 to 15 kl at R18,50 per kl is:
The last 7 kl of the 22 kl, charged at R26,40 per kl, cost:
The amount payable for 22 kl, including VAT at 15% on the consumption total of R351,30, is:
On the conventional option at 380 kWh, the total of consumption at R2,05 plus the R220,00 fixed charge is:
At 380 kWh, comparing prepaid at R948,00 with conventional at R999,00 shows:
At 600 kWh, prepaid costs R1 590,00 and conventional costs R1 450,00, so the better advice for a heavy user is:
options: Either option, since the totals are equal

questions.question: On a graph of cost against consumption for two tariff systems, the break-even point is where:
options: The two cost lines cross each other
The steeper line reaches the vertical axis
VAT is added to both totals

questions.question: On the price staircase, using more units in a month means:
options: Every unit you bought becomes more expensive
Each new unit may cost more, but earlier units keep their cheaper price
The municipality re-prices the whole month at the top rate

questions.question: Charging all 380 units at R2,60 instead of filling the blocks in order overcharges by:
The way to pay less on a rising block tariff is to:
options: Buy vouchers only at month end
Buy vouchers in several small amounts
Use fewer units so the month stays on the lower blocks

questions.question: The most expensive water in the lesson's household is:
options: The kilolitres above 15 kl, on the top block
All water costs the same per kilolitre

questions.question: Fixing a leak that wastes 7 kl a month saves, before VAT:
options: R184,80, because the wasted water sat on the top block
Nothing, because the first block is free

questions.question: VAT on the water consumption total of R351,30 comes to:
The first 6 kl are supplied free because:
options: The meter cannot measure below 6 kl
Households below 6 kl pay VAT only
The municipality forgets to bill small amounts
Basic water is treated as a right that must stay affordable

subtopics.title: Which Deal Is Cheaper for You

questions.question: The R220,00 fixed fee on the conventional option hurts small users most because:
options: Spread over few units, it adds more cost per unit

questions.question: At 600 kWh the conventional option wins because:
options: The fixed fee is waived for heavy users
The staircase rates fall at high usage
The flat R2,05 avoids the expensive top blocks of the staircase

questions.question: Below the break-even consumption, the cheaper choice in this lesson is:
options: Conventional, because of the fixed fee
Prepaid, whose cost line lies lower there

questions.question: A full-marks comparison answer must contain:
options: Only the name of the cheaper option
Both totals, the cheaper option, the saving, and advice tied to the household's usage
